questions.q: Olympiad Stage 1: If condition A is False and condition B is True, what does the expression `(A OR B)` evaluate to?
options: False
True
Zero
Syntax Error
questions.explanation: The OR operator requires only one condition to be True. Since B is True, `(A OR B)` evaluates to True.
questions.hint: Does OR need both conditions, or just at least one?

questions.q: Olympiad Stage 2: An automated school bell algorithm is written as: `IF (time == 13:00 AND is_weekend == False AND is_holiday == False): ring_bell()`. On Sunday at 13:00, will the bell ring?
options: Yes, because it is 13:00
No, because `is_weekend` is True on Sunday, so the condition `is_weekend == False` becomes False, stopping the AND expression
Yes, because bells love ringing on Sundays
No, because clocks stop working on weekends
questions.explanation: Since it is Sunday, `is_weekend` is True. The condition requires `is_weekend == False`. In an AND expression, one False makes the entire statement False.
questions.hint: Examine what happens to the AND condition when one of the three requirements fails.

questions.q: Olympiad Championship: Look at this logic gate combination: `Output = NOT (Sensor_A AND Sensor_B)`. If Sensor_A is 1 (True) and Sensor_B is 1 (True), what is the final Output?
options: 1 (True)
0 (False)
Undefined
questions.explanation: First evaluate inside the parentheses: `(1 AND 1)` equals 1 (True). Then apply the NOT operator: `NOT (True)` equals 0 (False). This is a NAND logic gate.
questions.hint: Evaluate the AND inside the parentheses first, then apply the NOT flip.
